session: 61GEMSDOE lane — buried structure, basement-depth steps from gravity inversion
scope: 3-5 candidates not previously implemented anywhere in the family; GitHub code search across org:buffedlizard55-lab returned 0 hits for 'oldenburg' and 0 for 'parker' and 4 for 'depth_to_base_surf' (all in 16GEMSDOE, used as raw channels only)

novelty_check.interpretation: No repository in the family has inverted the gravity layer. 16GEMSDOE uses iso_grav_anom and depth_to_base_surf as raw feature-stack channels and as a profile report only; neither is inverted and neither produces a basement-step product.

hypotheses.title: Parker-Oldenburg basement-depth steps
hypotheses.layers: band 13 iso_grav_anom (inverted); band 15 depth_to_base_surf (depth-scale calibration only)
hypotheses.signature: iterative Fourier inversion to basement relief, then non-maximum-suppressed maxima of the horizontal gradient of basement depth, with the throw of each step measured in metres across an 800 m aperture
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: A buried range-front or intrabasin normal fault offsets the basement surface even where alluvium hides the scarp, so the structure is in the gravity field but not in a surface-mapped catalogue. Alluvial cover is exactly the reason the catalogue misses it.
hypotheses.differs_from: No family repository inverts the gravity layer (code search: 0 hits for oldenburg/parker/inversion). Everyone else consumes the band as a channel.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: primary; measured on the holdout, see evidence/lane_experiments.json
hypotheses.cost: high (~20 min CPU): inversion, calibration grid search, step operator

hypotheses.title: Depth-dependent density contrast (Jachens & Moring compaction law)
hypotheses.layers: band 13 iso_grav_anom; published density-depth function 1900 / 2100 / 2300 / 2450 kg/m3 over 0-200 / 200-600 / 600-1200 / >1200 m (USGS OF 99-49 Table 1, after Jachens & Moring 1990)
hypotheses.signature: replace the single constant contrast with the layered law, i.e. invert for the sediment thickness whose own weight-dependent density is self-consistent; the correction grows with depth, so deep basin-margin steps sharpen relative to shallow ones
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Deep basins are precisely where cover is thickest and where the catalogue misses most. A constant contrast systematically under-estimates the depth of deep basins and therefore mis-positions their margins.
hypotheses.differs_from: H61-A uses one constant contrast. Nothing in the family uses a compaction law at all.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: moderate; fixes a known systematic in the deepest quartile, which is the lane's target domain
hypotheses.cost: medium (~40 min): an extra inner fixed-point loop on the density column

hypotheses.title: Step asymmetry: fault-controlled versus flexural drape
hypotheses.signature: the second derivative of depth across the crest; a fault offset is asymmetric (short steep limb on the downthrown side, long back-tilted limb), a draped or flexed margin is symmetric
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Suppresses the basin-margin flexures that produce gravity gradients without a fault, which is the main false-positive source for H61-A
hypotheses.differs_from: H61-A uses only the first derivative and is blind to this distinction
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: precision gain rather than recall gain; raises DTI by removing false-positive mass
hypotheses.cost: low (~5 min, reuses the H61-A field)

hypotheses.title: Multi-scale gravity-gradient edge focusing
hypotheses.signature: scale-normalised ridge response of the provided gradient products at several smoothing scales, i.e. an edge-focusing operator on the anomaly itself rather than on an inverted interface
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Edges of the anomaly are source edges. Where the anomaly edge is not a mapped structure it is a candidate buried contact; the provided gradient bands are already computed by the organiser and avoid the inversion's regularisation choices
hypotheses.differs_from: 16GEMSDOE's topographic/geophysical ridge baseline uses these channels inside a 35-channel stack; no repository builds a step/edge product from them or calibrates it
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: unknown; this is the natural control for whether the inversion is worth its cost

hypotheses.title: Independent basin-depth calibration reference (GP-1012)
hypotheses.layers: external: USGS Geophysical Investigations Map GP-1012 (Saltus & Jachens, 1995), 1:2,500,000
hypotheses.signature: replace the band-15 depth-scale reference with the map the lane prescribes
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: calibration only; it does not predict, it fixes the metres-per-mGal scale
hypotheses.differs_from: band 15 is the organiser's own derived product, so calibrating to it is partially circular
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: none directly; removes one irregularity and de-biases the depth scale
hypotheses.status: BLOCKED — external data not obtainable from this sandbox

external_source.name: Saltus, R.W., and Jachens, R.C., 1995, Gravity and basin-depth maps of the Basin and Range Province, western United States
external_source.series: U.S. Geological Survey Geophysical Investigations Map GP-1012

competing_explanation_for_the_whole_lane.name: lateral density contrast within pre-Tertiary basement
competing_explanation_for_the_whole_lane.mechanism: a granitic body against mafic volcanics, a hydrothermally altered zone, a caldera fill or a palaeo-weathered horizon changes the density laterally at constant basement depth, and its gravity expression is a step indistinguishable from a basement offset
competing_explanation_for_the_whole_lane.test: independent physics — a lithologic contact is a magnetic lineament, so a gravity step within 2 px of a reduced-to-pole magnetic contact crest is demoted (band 2 rtp)
competing_explanation_for_the_whole_lane.reference: Hildenbrand et al. 1999 (USGS OF 99-49) separates the isostatic residual field into a basement component (lateral basement density) and a basin component (thickness), which is the standard statement that both exist in the same field
